errors.description: The displayed definition makes μ identically zero because complex-number multiplication is commutative. Consequently Example 2.8 reduces its proposed real subspace to the line generated by [1] and its imaginary multiple, although [1] is in H^{1,0} and its conjugate must lie in the distinct, nonzero H^{0,1} component.
errors.evidence: The numerator is printed as (∫_{γ1}ω · ∫_{γ2}ω − ∫_{γ2}ω · ∫_{γ1}ω); Example 2.8 then uses μ in ℝ[(1 + μ·yD(x))/2] + √−1 ℝ[(1 + μ·yD(x))/2].

errors.location: Corollary 2.7, formulas for n even and n odd
errors.description: The claimed real subspace includes i[w_j], but w_j is the sum of a class and its asserted complex conjugate and is therefore fixed by conjugation; its imaginary multiple is anti-fixed and cannot be the image of a real cohomology class under the stated comparison. A conjugate-pair real basis needs the imaginary multiple of the difference of the pair.
errors.evidence: The corollary defines w_{j_i} = (y^i f_{j_i} + y^{n−1−i} f̃_{j_i})/2 and includes ℝ·[w_j] + ℝ·[√−1 w_j] in (φ_C⁻¹ ◦ P)(H^{n−1}_{prim}(X,ℝ)).

errors.description: The formula cannot determine the conjugate class in the stated generality: it chooses an arbitrary g and fixes a scalar by matching only the self-pairing with U_k. In a Hodge summand of dimension greater than one, identifying the conjugate requires its pairings against a full basis of the opposite summand; the hypotheses impose neither a dual-basis condition nor orthogonality, so the asserted multiple of arbitrary g need not be the conjugate.
errors.evidence: The theorem permits “any polynomial” y^{n−1−i}g with f_{j_i}g_{j_i} outside Jac(G), while the proof says finding the conjugate “amounts to finding h” with only R(y^i f_{j_i}, y^{n−1−i}h_{j_i}) = U_{k,γ}.

errors.location: Section 2.4, odd n, Definition of U_{k,γ} and proof of Theorem 2.3
errors.description: For the odd-n case the period-coordinate pairing uses the intersection matrix P directly, but periods on a homology basis give the cohomology cup-product matrix P⁻¹ (up to the orientation convention). Since the manuscript states det(P)=±e with e>1, P is not unimodular and P⁻¹ is not P in general. Thus P_X P overline(P_X)^T need not equal the cup-product pairing used in the proof, invalidating the odd-n construction.
errors.evidence: Section 2.4 states det(γ_α·γ_β)=±e and defines U_{k,γ} using (γ_i·γ_j), equivalently P_X·P·overline(P_X)^T; the proof identifies a cohomology class with the homology vector whose coefficients are its periods and then equates the resulting intersection pairing to ∫_X w∧overline{w}.
